'''Michael Levitt''', {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}}<ref name=frs/> ({{langx|he|מיכאל לויט}}; born 9 May 1947) is a South African-born [[biophysicist]] and a professor of [[structural biology]] at [[Stanford University]], a position he has held since 1987.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://csb.stanford.edu/ |title=Levitt Lab Server &#124; Computational Structural Biology |website=Csb.stanford.edu |access-date=22 March 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160325231210/http://csb.stanford.edu/ |archive-date=25 March 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://csb.stanford.edu/levitt/ |title=Michael Levitt |website=Csb.stanford.edu\accessdate=2017-03-22 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100715200937/http://csb.stanford.edu/levitt/ |archive-date=15 July 2010 }}</ref> Levitt received the 2013 [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]],<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/502280a| pmid = 24132265| title = Modellers react to chemistry award: Nobel Prize proves that theorists can measure up to experimenters| journal = [[Nature (journal)|Nature]]| volume = 502| issue = 7471| page = 280| year = 2013| last1 = Van Noorden | first1 = Richard|bibcode = 2013Natur.502..280V | doi-access = free}}</ref> together with [[Martin Karplus]] and [[Arieh Warshel]], for "the development of multiscale models for complex chemical systems".<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/nature.2013.13903| title = Computer modellers secure chemistry Nobels| journal = Nature| year = 2013| last1 = Van Noorden | first1 = R. | s2cid = 211729791}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release
 | title = The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2013
 | publisher = Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
 | date = 9 October 2013
 | url = https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/press-22.pdf
 | access-date = 17 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="NYT-20131009">{{cite news |last=Chang |first=Kenneth |title=3 Researchers Win Nobel Prize in Chemistry |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/10/10/science/three-researchers-win-nobel-prize-in-chemistry.html |date=9 October 2013 |work=The New York Times |access-date=9 October 2013 }}</ref><ref name=offnobel>{{cite web|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/chemistry/laureates/2013/levitt-facts.html |title=Michael Levitt – Facts |publisher=Nobelprize.org |date=9 May 1947 |access-date=22 March 2017}}</ref> In 2018, Levitt was a founding co-editor of the ''[[Annual Review of Biomedical Data Science]]''.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev-bd-01-041718-100001|title=What is Biomedical Data Science and do We Need an Annual Review of It?|year=2018|last1=Altman|first1=Russ B.|last2=Levitt|first2=Michael|journal=Annual Review of Biomedical Data Science|volume=1|pages=i-iii|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Michael Levitt was born in [[Pretoria]], South Africa, to a Jewish family from [[Plungė]], [[Lithuania]]; his father was from [[History of the Jews in Lithuania|Lithuania]] and his mother from the [[History of the Jews in the Czech Republic|Czech Republic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://en.delfi.lt/53464/foreign-minister-congratulates-litvak-levitt-on-winning-nobel-prize-201353464/ |title=Foreign Minister congratulates Litvak Levitt on winning Nobel PrizeThe Lithuania Tribune |website=en.delfi.lt |access-date=2 February 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131013182224/http://en.delfi.lt/53464/foreign-minister-congratulates-litvak-levitt-on-winning-nobel-prize-201353464/ |archive-date=13 October 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He attended Sunnyside Primary School and then [[Pretoria Boys High School]] between 1960 and 1962. The family moved to England when he was 15.<ref name="haaretz.com">{{cite web|last=Ravidyesterday |first=Barak |url=https://www.haaretz.com/2013-10-10/ty-article/.premium/levitt-after-nobel-win-i-have-no-ego/0000017f-e0c4-d38f-a57f-e6d671e20000 |title=Nobel laureate Michael Levitt tells Haaretz: 'I still feel 16, so I have no ego' – World |website=Haaretz |date=10 October 2013 |access-date=22 March 2017}}</ref> Levitt spent 1963 studying [[applied mathematics]] at the [[University of Pretoria]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://web.up.ac.za/default.asp?ipkCategoryID%3D8641%26ArticleID%3D18621 |title=News > University of Pretoria |access-date=30 October 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131101211033/http://web.up.ac.za/default.asp?ipkCategoryID=8641&ArticleID=18621 |archive-date=1 November 2013 }}</ref> He attended [[King's College London]], graduating with a [[British undergraduate degree classification#First-class honours|first-class honours]] degree in [[physics]] in 1967.<ref>{{cite web|title=King's College London Calendar: 1968–1969 Page 282|url=http://www.kingscollections.org/calendars/collection/1968-1969/page-282|website=King's Collections|access-date=12 September 2017}}</ref><ref name="whoswho"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://csb.stanford.edu/levitt/2_Page_CV.html |title=Michael Levitt 2 Page CV |website=Csb.stanford.edu |access-date=22 March 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322220938/http://csb.stanford.edu/levitt/2_Page_CV.html |archive-date=22 March 2012 }}</ref>

In 1967, he visited Israel for the first time. Together with his Israeli wife, Rina,<ref name=rina>{{cite web|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/chemistry/laureates/2013/levitt-photo.html |title=Michael Levitt – Photo Gallery |publisher=Nobelprize.org |access-date=22 March 2017}}</ref> a [[Multimedia|multimedia artist]], he left to study at [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]], where their three children were born. Levitt was a PhD student in [[Computational biology]] at [[Peterhouse, Cambridge]], and was based at the [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] from 1968 to 1972, where he developed a computer program for studying the conformations of molecules that underpinned much of his later work.<ref name="levittphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Michael|last=Levitt|title=Conformation analysis of proteins |publisher=University of Cambridge |year=1972 |url=https://www.repository.cam.ac.uk/handle/1810/252821|author-link=Michael Levitt (biophysicist)|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.463153}}|doi=10.17863/CAM.15942
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Peterhouse alumnus|url=http://www.cam.ac.uk/news/nobel-prize-in-chemistry-for-peterhouse-alumnus|publisher=University of Cambridge|access-date=11 October 2013|date=2013-10-10}}</ref>

==Career and research==
In 1979, he returned to Israel and conducted research at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in [[Rehovot]], becoming an Israeli citizen in 1980. He served in the [[Israel Defense Forces]] for six weeks in 1985. In 1986, he began teaching at [[Stanford University]], and since then has split his time between Israel and California.<ref name="haaretz.com"/> He went on to gain a research fellowship at [[Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge]].

From 1980 to 1987, he was Professor of Chemical Physics at the Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot. Thereafter, he served as Professor of Structural biology, at Stanford University, California.

*[[Royal Society]] Exchange Fellow, Weizmann Institute, Israel, 1967–68<ref>{{cite news |last=Fiske |first=Gavriel |date=9 October 2013 |title=3 Jewish professors – two of them Israeli – share 2013 Nobel Prize in chemistry |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/israeli-prof-arieh-warshel-shares-2013-nobel-prize-in-chemistry/ |work=The Times of Israel |access-date=12 November 2017}}</ref>
*Staff Scientist, [[MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology]], Cambridge, 1973–80
*Professor of Chemical Physics, Weizmann Institute, 1980–87 (dept. chair 1980–83)
*Professor of Structural Biology, Stanford University, 1987–present

===Industrial collaboration===
Levitt has served on the Scientific Advisory Boards of the following companies: Dupont Merck Pharmaceuticals, AMGEN, Protein Design Labs, Affymetrix, Molecular Applications Group, 3D Pharmaceuticals, Algodign, Oplon Ltd, Cocrystal Discovery, InterX, and [[StemRad|StemRad, Ltd]],.{{citation needed|date=November 2017}}

===COVID-19===

Levitt has been outspoken during the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic]], and made a number of wrong predictions on the disease's spread based on his own modelling.<ref name="Boodman">{{cite news |last1=Boodman |first1=Eric |title=He's a Stanford professor and a Nobel laureate. Critics say he was dangerously misleading on Covid |url=https://www.statnews.com/2021/05/24/stanford-professor-and-nobel-laureate-critics-say-he-was-dangerously-misleading-on-covid/ |access-date=13 September 2021 |work=Stat |date=24 May 2021}}</ref><ref name="StanfordD">{{cite news|last=Lloyd|first=Zenobia|title=Q&A: Michael Levitt on why there shouldn't be a lockdown, how he's been tracking coronavirus
|url=https://www.stanforddaily.com/2020/08/02/qa-michael-levitt-on-why-there-shouldnt-be-a-lockdown-how-hes-been-tracking-coronavirus/|access-date=18 December 2021|work=Stanford Daily}}</ref><ref name=latimeslevitt>{{cite news |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |title=Why this Nobel laureate predicts a quicker coronavirus recovery: 'We're going to be fine' |url=https://www.latimes.com/science/story/2020-03-22/coronavirus-outbreak-nobel-laureate}}</ref> On 18 March 2020, he predicted that Israel would see less than ten deaths from COVID-19, and on 25 July 2020, he incorrectly predicted that the outbreak in the U.S. would be over by the end of August 2020 with a total of fewer than 170,000 deaths.<ref name="pred_25_07_2020">{{cite web |last1=Levitt |first1=Michael |title=US Covid19 will be d one in 4 weeks |url=https://twitter.com/mlevitt_np2013/status/1287036738565738496?lang=en |via=Twitter |language=en}}</ref><ref name=Boodman/><ref>{{Cite web|title=Prof Michael Levitt: here's what I got wrong – The Post|url=https://unherd.com/thepost/prof-michael-levitt-heres-what-i-got-wrong/|access-date=2020-10-11|website=UnHerd|language=en-GB}}</ref> As of November 2021, the U.S. was recording COVID-19 deaths at the rate of about 1,000 per day,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/12/15/us/covid-deaths-united-states.html|date=15 December 2021|access-date=15 December 2021|work=The New York Times|title=Covid deaths in the United States surpass 800,000 |last1=Bosman |first1=Julie |last2=Harmon |first2=Amy |last3=Sun |first3=Albert |last4=Reynolds |first4=Chloe |last5=Cahalan |first5=Sarah }}</ref> while Israel has reported over 8,000 COVID-19 deaths since the start of the pandemic.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/israel-detects-case-coronavirus-variant-81403245|title=Israel warns of 'emergency' after detecting new virus strain|last=Krauss|first=Joseph|date=26 November 2021|work=ABC}}</ref>

Levitt has also raised concerns about potential damaging effects of [[COVID-19 lockdowns|COVID-19 lockdown]] orders on economic activity as well in increasing suicide and abuse rates,<ref name=StanfordD /> and has signed the [[Great Barrington Declaration]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Herd Immunity Is 'Pixie Dust Thinking,' Infectious Disease Expert Says|first=Robin|last=Young|url=https://www.wbur.org/hereandnow/2020/10/14/herd-immunity-coronavirus|access-date=18 December 2021|work=WBUR}}</ref> a statement supported by a group of academics advocating for alternatives to lockdowns which has been criticized by the [[World Health Organization|WHO]] and other public health organizations as dangerous and lacking in sound scientific basis.<ref name=Hilldozens>{{cite news|first=Jessie|last=Hellmann|url=https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/521159-dozens-of-public-health-groups-experts-blast-herd-immunity-strategy-backed |title=Dozens of public health groups, experts blast 'herd immunity' strategy backed by White House|newspaper=The Hill|date=15 October 2020|access-date=18 October 2020}}</ref><ref name=GuardianTedros>{{cite news|author=Staff and agencies in Geneva|date=12 October 2020|title=WHO chief says herd immunity approach to pandemic 'unethical'|newspaper=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/12/who-chief-says-herd-immunity-approach-to-pandemic-unethical|access-date=12 October 2020}}</ref>

Critics have expressed concern regarding Levitt's incorrect or potentially misleading predictions as well as his anti-lockdown positions, in part due to his status as a Nobel laureate and his large following on Twitter.<ref name=Boodman /><ref>{{cite news|first=Fishwick|last=Samuel|title='I've had emails calling me evil'... Meet the Covid scientists at war|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/health/coronavirus-scientists-at-war-a4569551.html|date=13 October 2020|work=Evening Standard|location=London}}</ref> [[Maia Majumder]], a computational epidemiologist at [[Harvard Medical School]], stated that "Michael Levitt has a huge, huge following, so this creates lots of problems when he’s tweeting something that may be misinformative."<ref name=Boodman /> [[Randy Schekman]], a 2013 [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]] winner, wrote of Levitt's expressed positions that "in this instance, I believe he crossed a boundary from data to public policy where the impact of his word as a Nobel laureate has undue influence."<ref name=Boodman />

===Awards and honors===

Biology Organization]]|location=Heidelberg|title=Michael Levitt EMBO profile|author=Anon|year=1983}}</ref> a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2001|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2001]],<ref name=frs>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117114241/https://royalsociety.org/people/michael-levitt-11810/ |archive-date=17 November 2015 |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/michael-levitt-11810/ |location=London  |title=Professor Michael Levitt FRS |publisher=Royalsociety.org |author=Anon|year=2001 }} One or more of the preceding }}}}</ref> and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2002,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/michael-levitt-u8kqr6/|title=Michael Levitt|website=Member |archive-date=20 February 2015 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Levitt holds South African, American, British and Israeli citizenship.

His wife Rina died on 23 January 2017.

He is the sixth Israeli to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in under a decade.<ref>{{cite news|last=Pileggi |first=Tamar |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/tiny-israel-a-nobel-heavyweight-especially-in-chemistry/ |title=Tiny Israel a Nobel heavyweight, especially in chemistry |newspaper=The Times of Israel |date=9 October 2013 |access-date=22 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Solomon |first=Shoshanna |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/two-americans-german-win-nobel-medicine-prize/ |title=Israelis lose out to US-German trio for Nobel medicine prize |newspaper=The Times of Israel |access-date=22 March 2017}}</ref>
